title: 1902 eruption of Mont Pelée
summary: On 8 May 1902 a pyroclastic flow from Mont Pelée on Martinique destroyed the city of Saint-Pierre. UNESCO gives 28,000 deaths in the minutes after the explosion and also says nearly 30,000, while Oregon State University gives 29,000. UNESCO calls it the deadliest volcanic event of the 20th century; it gave its name to the Pelean eruptive type.

uncertainty.note: 8 May 1902 is the destructive pyroclastic flow; UNESCO describes the wider eruption episode as running from 1902 to 1905.

as_recorded.value: the pyroclastic flow on May 8, 1902, led to the death of 28,000 people
May 8, 1902 eruption which killed 29,000 people and destroyed the city of St. Pierre

importance.justification: Deadliest volcanic eruption of the 20th century and a reference event in volcanology.

audience_note: This record describes a disaster that killed about 28,000 to 30,000 people, and the death toll is stated plainly.

sources.title: Volcanoes and Forests of Mount Pelée and the Pitons of Northern Martinique

reviewer_note: Pin is the town of Saint-Pierre (Wikidata), where the destruction occurred; the volcano summit is about 7 km north. Death-toll sources disagree (28,000 and "nearly 30,000" inside the UNESCO page; 29,000 at Oregon State), so the summary gives all three. UNESCO page read via script fetch (WebFetch returned 403).
